text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Despite official announcments that the new municipal budget for Windhoek would not bring with it any major tariff adjustments, inhabitants of the capital will be bombarded with a wide range of increases for services, some by as much as 47 percent.
- The market for unleaded fuel in Namibia is expected to rise by as much as 35 percent within the next year compared to South Africa where only about 10 percent of drivers use lead-free petrol.

- During the short budget debate at the Windhoek city council, councillor Gunter Kaschik explained that the bus service will always prove a headache for the council. He requested Transnamib to look into the possibility of a city rail on the north-south axis of Windhoek.

- The Socio-Economic Integration Programme for Ex-combatants (SIPE), introduced two months ago, has been tasked with looking after the social integration of former soldiers from Plan, Koevoet and the SWATF, creating jobs for those that are handicapped due to combat.
